name: Mabe Fratti
label: Unheard of Hope
lede: Mabe Fratti learned cello in a Guatemalan church orchestra, took a three-month residency in Mexico and never really left. In 2024 Pitchfork ranked Sentir Que No Sabes No. 20 on its albums of the year.

eras.title: Saxophone denied, cello assigned
eras.text: Mabe Fratti grows up in a neo-pentecostal Guatemalan household with classical lessons, church-orchestra duty and a Ligeti CD her father brought home. The secular world reaches her through file-sharing and Soundcloud.

years.src: Loud and Quiet · Sounds and Colours · Wikipedia: Mabe Fratti
years.h: She wants the saxophone; her lungs pick the cello
years.p: Respiratory trouble ends the saxophone. At eight she lands on cello in the children's orchestra tied to Guatemala's national Sinfónica.
years.xp:
Loud and Quiet reports the respiratory problems. Sounds and Colours says her cello teacher was an "extreme evangelical Christian obsessed with the apocalypse, and an amazing player," who taught nothing written after 1900. In Fratti's words: "no minimalism, no experimentation."

Wikipedia gives her birth date as February 13, 1992, and adds that her current cello was a gift from her school.

years.src: Loud and Quiet · Wikipedia: Mabe Fratti
years.h: A Ligeti CD turns up between the wolf-howl records
years.p: Her father's disc piles run from Christian music and Disney to new age albums of animal sounds. One is by György Ligeti, and she is about ten.
years.xp:
Fratti told Loud and Quiet her father picked it out with "Oh this is for Mabe!" and that her reaction on hearing it was "What the fuck is this!"

Wikipedia adds that she later found a Jacqueline du Pré DVD on her own and began composing as a teenager.

q: I guess there was no demon inside me. I was exorcised.
years.src: Loud and Quiet · Sounds and Colours · Wikipedia: Mabe Fratti
years.h: Orchestra on Sundays, LimeWire at night
years.p: Fratti's neo-pentecostal church and evangelical school treat Yu-Gi-Oh as satanic. Online she finds reggae, blues and funk.
years.xp:
Loud and Quiet reports the community disapproved of secular interests and that church members believed she had a demon. She tells it with a shrug and a joke about being exorcised. Wikipedia says she found broader music through LimeWire and eventually left the church.

She told Sounds and Colours she began playing in bands in her late teens and that her parents remain very conservative.

eras.title: A residency that doesn't end
eras.text: A Goethe-Institut residency drops Fratti in Mexico, then Mexico City, where the experimental venues and the DIY scene change what a cellist is allowed to do. A first record follows.

years.big: "I went for three months and ended up staying six years… and counting."
years.src: Loud and Quiet · Sounds and Colours · Wikipedia: Mabe Fratti
years.h: A Goethe-Institut rep finds her on Soundcloud
years.p: Fratti's line to Sounds and Colours in 2021. The offer was a paid residency in Malinalco; from there she moved on to Mexico City.
years.xp:
She told the same interviewer the move "liberated me." She credits Mexico City venues such as Jazzorca and Terraza Monstruo, and the DIY scene around them, with the awakening; back home, she says, Guatemala was "so religious."

Wikipedia says she soon worked with Libertad Figueroa, Gudrun Gut and Julián Bonequi, and met Héctor Tosta and the future members of [[Amor Muere|92d31114-8a7a-4950-a855-985068f9df1c]].

years.src: Wikipedia: Mabe Fratti · Loud and Quiet
years.h: First album Pies Sobre La Tierra takes its cue from Sebald
years.p: Wikipedia says W. G. Sebald's The Rings of Saturn inspired it. Loud and Quiet says it came out on Hole Records, Tajak's label.
years.xp: Fratti describes her recordings as journal entries documenting moments in her life, per Loud and Quiet.

eras.title: Written in lockdown, recorded dry
eras.text: Lockdown writing turns into a run of records with guests from Berlin to Milwaukee. By Se Ve Desde Aquí she is skipping overdubs and cutting the reverb.

years.src: Sounds and Colours · Wikipedia: Mabe Fratti
years.h: Lockdown writing becomes Será Que Ahora Podremos Entendernos
years.p: Claire Rousay guests on "Hacia El Vacío" and Tajak plays on the record, per Wikipedia.
years.xp: Sounds and Colours calls it an album written in lockdown that has since had a new life, played live by the trio across the world. BBC 6 Music's Mary-Anne Hobbs has said Fratti plays cello like a wild angel.

years.h: Fratti and Concepción Huerta cut the Estática EP
years.p: Sounds and Colours dates it to late November 2021, on SA Recordings. Pitchfork praised its ecstatic synth riffs and unselfconscious bowing.
years.xp: The EP came out of sessions with Huerta, a pianist from Mexico. Sounds and Colours quotes Pitchfork's line: "The record blooms with ecstatic synth riffs and unselfconscious bowing."

q: I wanted it to sound dryer and dryer.
years.src: The Quietus · Levi Dayan · Wikipedia: Mabe Fratti
yt: KEXP session: No Se Ve Desde Acá
years.h: Se Ve Desde Aquí skips the overdubs and the reverb
years.p: No vocal or cello overdubs, and about $2,000 on microphones. Oneohtrix Point Never called the record mind blowing, per Wikipedia.
years.xp:
The Quietus reports the record came out on Tin Angel Records, with Tosta, drummer Gibrán Andrade, saxophonist Jarrett Gilgore and violinist Alina Maldonado among the players, and Exploded View's Hugo Quezada producing. Fratti mixed her own records and told the magazine the sound kept getting drier.

Levi Dayan's interview adds that the album leaned on long improvisations and hard editing, with wind arrangements by Tosta.

eras.title: Titanic, and No. 20
eras.text: Héctor Tosta, the guitarist and producer who records as I. la Católica, becomes Fratti's co-writer in Titanic and the producer of her fourth solo album. Pitchfork puts that album on its year-end list.

years.src: Wikipedia: Mabe Fratti · The Quietus · Loud and Quiet
years.h: Fratti, Concepción Huerta and two others become Amor Muere
years.p: The four-member collective, with Gibrana Cervantes and Camille Mandoki, makes A Time to Love, a Time to Die. Fratti had met some of them after moving to Mexico City.

years.src: Tin Angel Records: Titanic's Vidrio · BOMB Magazine · Loud and Quiet
yt: Live at Cafe OTO, London, Aug 2023
years.h: Fratti and Tosta debut as Titanic with Vidrio
years.p: Eight songs of chamber pop and jazz on Tin Angel Records. Tosta plays multiple instruments; Fratti writes the string arrangements and sings lead.
years.xp:
Tin Angel's release post says the Guardian placed it somewhere between jazz and chamber pop. BOMB Magazine later described the duo's work as effortlessly poised and endlessly ambitious.

The credit reads Titanic, I. la Católica and Mabe Fratti.

years.cap: Mabe Fratti with her cello, c. 2024
years.src: Wikipedia: Sentir Que No Sabes · Exclaim! · Treble · The Line of Best Fit
years.h: Pitchfork gives Sentir Que No Sabes an 8.4
years.p: The Guardian makes it album of the week. The record is out on Unheard of Hope.
years.xp:
Wikipedia lists I. La Católica as producer and arranger, with Jacob Wick on trumpet, Gibrán Andrade on drums and Estrella del Sol on whistle. It has a Metacritic score of 86 from ten critics.

Exclaim! hears opener "Kravitz" as a groovy distorted cello stomp; Treble hears horn stabs over an upright bass groove. The Line of Best Fit gave the album 7/10 and found it darker and more industrial than her earlier work.

years.src: Album of the Year · Pitchfork's 50 Best Albums of 2024 · Le Guess Who?
yt: Live at Le Guess Who?, Utrecht, Nov 9, 2024
years.h: Loud and Quiet makes it No. 3 of 2024
years.p: The Guardian has it at 12, Resident Advisor 10, Paste 17, Beats Per Minute 20 and Pitchfork 20, per Album of the Year. In November she plays it at Le Guess Who? in Utrecht, with the string quintet Shards.
years.xp: The Le Guess Who? set at TivoliVredenburg's Ronda on November 9 had Héctor Tosta on guitar and Gibrán Andrade on drums, and ran through "Kravitz," "No Se Ve Desde Acá" and "Desde el Cielo." Crack Magazine wrote that the lineup went from Fratti's crystalline vocals over razor-sharp drums to Tosta's guitar shredding.

eras.title: Hagen, then the road
eras.text: Titanic follow up with a second album and a long European run, including dates supporting Black Country, New Road.

years.src: Stereogum · BOMB Magazine · Tin Angel Records: Titanic announce HAGEN
yt: Mabe Fratti: Desde El Cielo, Live on KEXP
years.h: Daniel Lopatin plays synth on Titanic's Hagen
years.p: Lopatin and Nate Salon play synths on "Pájaro de fuego"; drummer Eli Keszler improvises on "Gotera".
years.xp: Stereogum says the album came out on Unheard of Hope, with "Gotera" as lead single; the song began during a Gaudeamus residency in the Netherlands. BOMB praised Fratti's vocal on "La dueña" as career-best.

years.src: Tin Angel Records: Titanic announce HAGEN
years.h: Titanic play End of the Road, then support Black Country, New Road
years.p: The fall tour of the UK and Europe runs through October 31, with [[Black Country, New Road|e9403d9c-329b-4108-a26f-564159d441d9]] on select dates.
